text:
kevin: quick check — I ran a sweep across the staging fleet to see p95/p99 tradeoffs for different max_wait_ms vs max_batch_tokens combos. sharing top-level notes.
anya: nice, curious what microbatch_size you used and whether KV cache hit-rate changed.
kevin: microbatch_size=4 mostly, some runs with 2 and 8. KV/cache config unchanged. dataset = 10k short prompts + 2k long prompts (avg 300 tokens).
devon: what hardware?
kevin: A100-40GB, mixed precision, kernel selector on. used runtime branch: perf/scheduler-sweep-2026. infra-bot: benchmark job 1768123456 started — logs at https://ci.internal/bench/1768123456
sara: top-level numbers?
kevin: summary:
- max_wait_ms=5, max_batch_tokens=4096 => best throughput but p99 spikes ~1.9x vs baseline
- max_wait_ms=20, max_batch_tokens=2048 => balanced, p95 within SLO, p99 ~1.2x
- max_wait_ms=50, max_batch_tokens=1024 => lowest tail but throughput drops ~18%
- fallback to smaller kernels triggered when batch tokens > 6k cumulatively => kernel switch cost ~4-6ms per batch
anya: interesting. how did prefix/KV cache behave on long prompts?
kevin: cache hit-rate dropped ~7% at high max_batch_tokens because batching grouped different contexts and evicted more KV entries. p99 correlated with KV miss churn.
devon: can you paste perf snippet from flamegraph/profile?
kevin: sure, paste:
```
# flame summary (avg of slow tails)
runtime_total_ms: 120
kernel_exec_ms: 78
kv_lookup_ms: 12
kernel_switch_overhead_ms: 6
scheduler_queue_ms: 18
```
anya: kernel_switch_overhead is concerning. is selector threshold too tight? maybe prefer single fast kernel for mixed seq lengths.
sara: did you try adaptive max_wait (deps on inflight qlen)?
kevin: yes — lightweight rule: if inflight_tokens < 2 * avg_seq -> max_wait=5 else =30. that reduced p99 by ~10% vs static 20ms for this workload, throughput ~2% down.
devon: any regression vs previous release?
kevin: compared to v2026.01 baseline: we see 6% higher p99 for tails when using large max_batch_tokens with static max_wait_ms=5. suspect combination of kernel fallback + KV churn.
anya: thoughts on mitigation?
sara: options:
- cap max_batch_tokens lower for heterogeneous seq workloads (auto-detect)
- increase microbatch_size prioritize same-context grouping
- avoid kernel fallback by widening compatibility in fast kernel or do faster fallback path
- tweak KV eviction policy to prefer keeping recent prefixes
kevin: I prototyped a quick heuristic: prefer batching by prefix-hash bucket first (500ms bucketing window) then fill to max_batch_tokens. result: KV hit-rate up 5%, p99 down 12% but throughput down 8%.
devon: sounds promising. need to check fairness for small requests.
anya: can we emit a runtime metric: batch_kernel_switch_count + kv_misses_per_batch so ops can alert on this pattern?
kevin: already added counters in the branch. infra-bot: deploy perf/scheduler-sweep-2026 to staging
sara: next steps: (1) run targeted sweep for microbatch_size = 2,4,8 with prefix-bucket batching; (2) test adaptive max_wait heuristic under bursty arrival; (3) validate on p95/p99 SLOs end-to-end. assign owners?
kevin: I'll take (1) and (2).
anya: I'll validate KV policy changes (3) and run longer soak.
devon: I'll do kernel selector audit — see if we can remove one fallback path or speed it up.
kevin: thanks. will push updated perf logs to the benchmark URL and open a follow-up thread with condensed numbers.
anya: :thumbsup:
sara: +1
infra-bot: job 1768123456 finished, artifacts uploaded: /artifacts/1768123456
